articleTitle: Estimation of pressure field and maximum velocity of an oseen vortex
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this work tangential velocity and pressure field have been calculated for a lamb-oseen vortex. The maximum tangential velocity as a function of time has also been calculated. Moreover, effects of time and core radius on velocity and pressure profile have been analyzed. The effects of variation of density, viscosity and circulation on the velocity of vortex have also been discussed and different combinations of these parameters have been plotted using computer codes and MATLAB. The Navier strokes equations in polar coordinates have been used for the derivation of velocity and pressure field. Similarity solution has also been derived for the velocity of the vortex. The graphs have helped us to observe the change in behavior of tangential velocity of an oseen-vortex as different parameters are changed. Three mediums have been analyzed i-e air, water and blood. The calculation of pressure field has also been validated through experimental results. For this purpose, the forced vortex apparatus has been used and medium selected is water. The pressure field calculated would also help us in studying the variations of pressure as a function of time and radius. The expression derived for the maximum tangential velocity would help us in understanding the decay of tangential velocity with time and core radius and would allow us to calculate the maximum tangential velocity using any given system parameters.

articleTitle: BOM technology based knowledge service mechanism in aircraft product development process
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Knowledge plays a significant role during product development process. The knowledge service mechanism is the key stage for the organization and usage of design knowledge. This paper approaches the mechanism by BOM (Bill of material) technology to organize and reuse design knowledge. Firstly, the knowledge BOM is put forwards and constructed based on the product BOM, hence the effective organization of knowledge is realized. Secondly, according to the refinement and evolution process of product BOM, a knowledge task meta model is constructed to describe the design task, and the mechanism of knowledge integration into the task is formulized to achieve the knowledge service for product development. Finally, an aircraft part, a wing part structural design process is taken as an example to verify the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of toxoplasmosis disease transmission dynamics
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Numerical modeling is a tool to provide reliable discretizations for continuous non-linear dynamical systems. Present work deals with the numerical modeling of Toxoplasmosis disease dynamics in a population. A competitive numerical scheme for the dynamics of Toxoplasmosis disease has been proposed. A comparison of proposed scheme with already existing standard finite difference schemes is also presented. Standard finite difference schemes provide conditional convergence while the proposed numerical scheme is unconditionally convergent and remains consistent with the biological nature of continuous dynamical system for all values of the parameters.

articleTitle: Effect of heat transfer on the flow of herschel-bulkley fluid in a compliant channel with peristalsis: Peristaltic transport of herschel-bulkley fluid
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The present study discusses the peristaltic flow of Herschel-Bulkley fluid in a two-dimensional flexible channel. The heat transfer effects are also considered and the analysis has been done by taking a non-uniform channel into account. Analytical expressions of solution have been obtained using long wavelength analysis. Influence of various emerging parameters has been sketched and discussed through graphs.

articleTitle: Use of physiological biomarker for detection of level of infection in experimental animals
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Pakistan has an agricultural economy. Livestock is an important sector of agriculture contributing approximately 58.6 percent to the agriculture value added and 11.6 percent to the overall GDP during 2015-16. Antibiotic resistance is emerging problem in Pakistan. Bacteria have deleterious effects on livestock production and antibiotic resistance even worsen the situation. Keeping in view this problem the study designed for the comparative study of Ceftiofur free crystalline and Ceftiofur (HCL) to control the bacterial disease caused by E. coli and Staphylococcus aureus with simultaneous comparison of physiological biomarker C-reactive protein values. Increased C-reactive protein value suggesting underlying infection as a result of inflammation is used as an innovative tool in this study. The study carried out on the 8 Specific Pathogen Free (SPF) Indian rabbits as the research model. The physiological parameters i.e. temperature, respiration rate etc. were taken before the inoculation of the bacteria. All the samples were collected at an interval of 24hrs; once before applying treatment, secondly after inoculating the desired bacteria up to 192 hours and thirdly after application of the treatment i.e. Ceftiofur Free Crystalline and Ceftiofur (HCL). All freshly collected blood samples will be checked for C-reactive protein using HumaTex CRP kit. This is an agglutinations based test using goat antibodies and serum extracted from the blood of research model i.e. rabbit. The semi-quantitative results showed that C-reactive protein (CRP) values were normal for first 72 hours in all rabbits then showed an increase to 48mg/l at 96th hours and after that rabbits which were inoculated with E. Coli had maximum 96-mg/l C-reactive protein (CRP) value and those with Staplococcus aureus had 192mg/l after 120 hours These values were persistent till application of the treatment i.e. after 192 hours. After application of the treatment with Ceftiofur Free Crystalline 1.1mg/kg body wiegh tid I/M E. coli inoculated rabbit's value dropped down to normal within 24 hours and that of Staphlococcus aureus inoculated rabbit's showing 96mg/l after 24<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> hours, 48mg/L after 48 hours and then dropped down to normal. Those rabbits which were treated with Ceftiofur (HCL) single dose 2.2mg/kg body weigh I/M showed persistently increased values for first 48 hours and then dropped down as; E. coli 96mg/l at 96<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> hours, 48mg/l at 120<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> hours and after 168 hours became normal, Staphlococcus aureus 96mg/l after 72 hours, 48mg/l after 120 hours and this 48mg/L was persistent till the end. These results confirm that Ceftiofur Free Crystalline has significantly greater efficacy than Ceftiofur (HCL) for E. coli and Staphylococcus aureus and physiolological biomarker C-reactive protein can be used as a diagnostic tool to find out underlying infection.

articleTitle: Technique for the detection of human pathogen via maintenance of leishmania promastigote in blood agar culture medium
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Leishmaniasis is vector borne protozoan parasitic disease caused by Leishmania species. The disease affects the exposed parts of body causing acute inflammatory changes for example itching, redness, edema and discharge of body fluids etc. Its vector is sand fly. This protozoan is endemic in many parts of tropical and subtropical areas. This disease is prevalent in all four provinces of Pakistan, including Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Baluchistan and Sindh. In vitro cultivation and maintenance of Leishmania parasite are known methods for the disease diagnosis thereby helping in treatment of the Leishmaniasis disease. In the present study a simple and cheap blood agar based biphasic culture medium is described, which is capable of supporting long time cultivation of Leishmania promastigotes in vitro. This culture can be used for the screening and further detection of Leishmania parasite in both animals and humans. If this disease is not treated timely and accurately this may lead to secondary infection, permanent scars on the face or other parts of the body and/ or patient may become handicap resulting in loss of working hours. The blood agar culture medium used in present study can be prepared with cost effective ingredients in comparison to other available culture media that are quite expensive. Through this method we can obtain a large number of organisms that can also be used in serological studies and molecular identification. In far-flung areas of Pakistan the diagnostic facilities are not available therefore we have developed here a cheaper method for the cultivation and detection of Leishmaniasis.

articleTitle: Comparison of APRI, FIB-4 and fibro test in prediction of fibrosis and cirrhosis in patients with hepatitis C
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Aspartate aminotransferase platelet ratio index (APRI), Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) and Fibro test are noninvasive methods to assess liver fibrosis. The objective of this study is to analyze the diagnostic performance of these tests for assessment of hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis during hepatitis C infection. Data for comparison of significant fibrosis and cirrhosis was obtained through earlier studies where the degree of fibrosis and cirrhosis was measured in accordance with METAVIR and Ishak scoring system. 52 studies analyzing APRI, FIB-4 and Fibro test for various stages of fibrosis in hepatitis C patients were assessed. The area under the SROC curves of the APRI, FIB-4 and Fibro test to estimate fibrosis were 0.7736, 0.7163, and 0.8921 respectively while the areas under SROC curves of the APRI, FIB-4 and Fibro test to predict cirrhosis were 0.8244, 0.8167, and 0.9422, respectively. Fibro test is better than others in estimating both presence and absence of fibrosis and cirrhosis.

articleTitle: Software application for QTS24 test strip
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The API (Analytical Profile Index) - a well-established method for bacterial identification to the species level-is a bacterial classification based on biochemical tests On the same grounds, QTS24 test trip (an indigenous gramve test strip) was developed by CESAT for the identification of bacteria organisms which has shown promising comparative results with API. The test strip contains 24 bacterial identification tests which are comparatively more in numbers than API. In QTS24 test strip, the process of bacterial identification is based on the positive and negative laboratory test results of the test strip which can be interpreted by manual interpretation dichotomous elimination tree/key<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2]</sup> This simplifies the bacterial identification procedure while working with the loads of isolates in the lab. To further aid the interpretation and recording of results, an easy to install windows based software application for QTS-24 Test Strips has been developed. This software application will automate the interpretation dichotomous elimination tree / key technique to further simplify the procedure of working with loads of isolates in the lab. The software application accepts the positives and negative lab results of QTS strip for 27 biochemical tests to identify 75 different organisms of bacteria. QTS software application features include, logging of interpretation results into database, searching of logged results, modification and deletion of logged results. It also features on taking backup of logged result database and restoring the old database of logged results back into software application. Display of 75 nomenclature and percentage positivity and negativity pivot chart is further added to the software application features. The software application is developed in Microsoft Technologies at front and Microsoft SQL Compact database at the backend to store the process results.

articleTitle: Study of gender preference of hepatitis virus in suspected patients from Islamabad and Karachi (Southern and northern parts of Pakistan)
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In the developing countries including Pakistan, hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) cause serious health problems. A range of risk factors are responsible for this infectious disease's spread. This study was carried out to detect virus type in suspected patients from Islamabad and Karachi (Southern and Northern parts of Pakistan) and evaluate the viral association with gender. Identification of viral hepatitis type was done by real time PCR (Cepheid, USA). Association of Hepatitis viruses (Hepatitis B & C) infection with gender was analyzed, among suspected patients reported in a Local Hospital of Karachi and Islamabad. A total of 916 suspected patients were screened for Hepatitis B (n=282) and Hepatitis C (n=634). Total pervasiveness of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C was found to be more common in male by percentage analysis but statistical analysis results differ from these. Further studies are needed to characterize HBV and HCV viruses, causes of their spread and transmission with reference to Pakistan.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics based design of hull and propeller of an underwater vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Underwater Vehicles are now used widely for mining, marine research, and military surveillance etc. Design of the vehicle is of paramount importance as efficiency of the mechanical equipment is one of the important areas of research these days. A little increase in efficiency can help saving a large amount of fuel, and consequently, decreasing amount of money required to be spent and weight of vehicle. Design study of the vehicle may be carried out by performing a parametric study related to the hydrodynamics of the vehicle. Considering the geometric and kinematic characteristics of the blades and the hull, this study aims to figure out a configuration for greater hydrodynamic efficiency of the vehicle. Since real-time experimental equipment is expensive, we adopted a computational approach. For the present study, simulations for incompressible viscous flow over the underwater vehicle through a finite-volume method based industrial flow solver-ANSYS Fluent were employed. During the simulations, we swept over a parametric space consisting of hull shape, aspect ratio of the vehicle, and Reynold's number.

articleTitle: Particles order-disorder in complex (yukawa) fluids using molecular dynamics simulations
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The measurements of the particle order-disorder (OD-structures) structures of a complex material based on general numerical experiments using a model pair, Yukawa interaction potential, which approximates real interactions in this material. The results obtained for a complex system (dusty plasmas) with interparticle connections depending on plasma parameters (Γ, κ). The particle OD results are calculated through homogenous nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations (HNEMD) for a series of various criterions of plasma parameters. In comparison to present results, the size system does not disturb significantly the arrangements of the particle OD but the long-range computation shows alterations toward high (Γ) by an augmentation of (κ). It has been shown that the presented approach is an alternative method to employ for computing the long-range alignment in dusty plasmas. It is so much competent for assembly the HNEMD and can be castoff to envisage the OD-structures in complex (Yukawa) fluids.

articleTitle: A 20W single-input doherty power amplifier's bandwidth extension for wireless communication
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this paper, a single-input Doherty power amplifier for wireless communication application in the 2.4 GHz frequency band are presented. Main goal of this study is to improve the performance of gallium-nitride (GaN) Doherty transmitters over wide bandwidth in the 2.4 GHz frequency band. For this purpose, the linearity-efficiency trade-off for the proposed architecture is discussed. Simulated results demonstrate that the single-input Doherty power amplifier exhibited a peak drain efficiency (DE) of 77% and 6 dB back-off efficiency 47% at designed frequency. The simulated results showed saturated output power more than 42.2 dBm throughout the designed band. Saturated efficiency and small-signal gain of the proposed DPA is higher than 60% and 10dB, respectively. On the other side, proposed single-input Doherty power amplifier has lower linearity.

articleTitle: Analysis of distribution of feed water through J tubes in feed water ring of chashma nuclear power plant
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In a typical pressurized water reactor's (PWR) steam generator, the primary component for distribution of feed water in secondary side is feed water ring. In this research, computational fluid dynamics analyses are carried out to determine the flow as well as pressure distribution in feed water ring with J tube. Furthermore, velocity contour at the J tube and feed water ring junction has been plotted. It was concluded that the junction is subjected to erosion-corrosion because of a higher erosion velocity through those tubes. So, by moving these tubes to other locations can increase the life of feed water ring. The flow distribution of feed water ring of Chashma nuclear power plant was also compared with other kinds of headers used. A modified design of feed water ring was suggested. The modifications resulted in a decreased erosion-corrosion risk on the surface of feed water ring. Additionally, the performance of feed water ring in main feed water line break accident was also carried out, reverse flow observed before closure of check valve was 1154 kg/sec. A pressure surge of 52 MPa was observed after the closure of check valve, which may result in water hammering and can damage the feed water ring.

articleTitle: Evaluation of thrust from a multi-nozzle output device with single input
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: A multi-nozzle output device with a single input, is designed and optimized using Computational Fluid Dynamics techniques and thrust is evaluated. In this regard a platform, having required number of nozzles is designed and using a distribution chamber, working fluid is supplied to each nozzle efficiently, maximizing the net thrust developed. Using a 3D modeling software, the geometry is created and imported to a commercial CFD code. A non-structured grid having tetrahedral elements is generated to investigate the fluid flow. An additional fluid domain is used to analyze the fluid flow after leaving the nozzles. Pressure difference maintained to generate the fluid flow is determined by optimizing the nozzles iteratively. Incompressible air is used as working fluid with k-epsilon turbulence model. Steady state simulations with different mesh sizes are performed to achieve a grid independent solution. By reducing the weight of device and controlling the distribution of fluid in different nozzles, optimization is performed to maximize the thrust. Taking into consideration, the Mach number, noise of fluid ejecting from nozzles is reduced. Device is designed to lift the additional weight. A device capable of carrying such amount of weight with fluid ejecting at low Mach number is one of its own kind and find its application in silent rapid movements without any considerable disturbance in its wake.

articleTitle: A unique framework of assembly design combining tolerance and regression analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Innovative product development has become highly demanding and challenging in the current era. Products are getting more sophisticated with time and it is indispensable to be extremely heedful as far as product variation assessment is concerned. In order to develop a quality product right for the first time, it is imperative to calculate variation early at the design stage. This very fact is highly important for gear based precise assemblies as gears possess a dynamic feature towards rotation. For such a precise rotation, at first there is a need to determine the significant variation contributor, and afterwards it is mandatory to verify the impact of variation. Tons of literature has been published on tolerancing and its effects on assemblies yet there is lack of research regarding practical implementation and validation of tolerancing. In this research, a novel idea of tolerance simulation along with its merger with regression analysis has been presented. The results of the tolerance simulation have further been processed and a relationship has been developed for rotational accuracy assessment. Proposed idea would open new doors of combining tolerancing and regression analysis vis-à-vis many industrial applications.

articleTitle: Computational fluid dynamics analysis of IPMC actuated mechanical fin through two-way fluid structure interaction approach
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Experimental methods being used to investigate hydrodynamics of biomimetic micro-robots under specific associated conditions are limited because of their inability to measure certain parameters such as spatial velocity, pressure, surface pressure and stress distribution in their structures. These limitations are being overcome through advanced approaches of computational modeling. In this manuscript, a numerical simulation is performed to carry out computational fluid dynamics of ionic polymer metal composite, an electroactive polymer, displaced fin of a towed fish. Fin's non-linear displacement disturbs the fluid field dynamically. Fluid receives fin's non-linear displacement and consequential forces employed by the fluid act on it which makes it a two-way problem. Analysis systems of ANSYS mechanical and CFX flow are coupled in ANSYS WORKBENCH to perform this multi-field numerical simulation. Dynamics of the disturbed fluid field is studied for complete actuation cycle of the fin. Hydrodynamic forces acting on the assembly components are depicted. Moreover, strategies on mesh refinement through improved techniques are studied. Von-Mises stress in the fin and pressure coefficients of the wing and fin are also investigated. Same methodology is applicable to self-propelled devices.

articleTitle: Effects of variation in flow field on store separation
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper focuses on the effects of variation in Mach number and angle of attack on store separation trajectories of external stores for typical combat aircraft. Multiple cases of variable flight parameters were analyzed to simulate various flight attitudes and velocities of the aircraft. A generic test case of a cropped delta wing with a standard air to ground store was taken as reference and the time dependent Euler and Navier Stokes equations were employed to solve the 6 DoF equations of motion in ANSYS Fluent®. A User Defined Function was used to incorporate the influence of thrusters in the computational analyses. Motion of the store was realized by integrating dynamic meshes in the computational domain. This arrangement enables to accommodate the displacement of store in the flow field. A standard test case was taken as reference to compare with the available literature, while several other test cases were developed to analyze the variation in trajectories due to flow field alteration. The result of the baseline test case was in complete agreement the literature data. Subsequent test cases depicted a complete profile of store behavior in altering flight regimes. The unrestricted movement of a store, coupled with the ejector and gravitational forces, is in complete coherence with the basic aerodynamic fundamentals of a free falling body in the flow field. Moreover, the variation in flight parameters also depicts a consistency in the variation in store release trajectories. The current research can prove beneficial for the prediction of release trajectories on any platform carrying a similar store.

articleTitle: E-shape patch antenna for 4G, LTE and S-band applications
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Patch miniaturization is an ongoing trend in modern communication technology nowadays. In this paper functional behavior of E slotted patch is presented. With additional ground irregularities multi resonating frequency response is attained at range of 1–8GHZ resulting at most gain of 2.82dB −4.23dB, directivity in 5.21dBi-4.05dBi range with good impedance bandwidth. With use of fractal patch technique FR4 is chosen as substrate bases. With help of implementing shortening pin technique reduction of antenna is accomplished to 74.15%. By changing location of shortening pin only different desired bands resonation can be achieved. This type of microstrip antenna has applications in mobile phone for 4G, LTE, CDMA, S-Band, L-Band and C-Band applications.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a hybrid frequency conversion assembly
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a Frequency Conversion Assembly for downconversion of an input signal in the 6-18GHZ range to 750MHz IF with a bandwidth of 400MHz. The assembly is based on Hybrid technology in that it contains both packaged and bare-chip components. The paper presents a description of the design methodology. Fabrication and testing steps have also been outlined. Test results have been observed to be in good agreement with the design parameters. Gain with flatness 3±3dB was achieved throughout the band with input VSWR<;2.5, as desired.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of breathing in a long blunt nosed body at supersonic speed
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: High speed aerodynamic bodies are associated with high aerodynamic drag. Reduction of this drag is a necessary requirement, for which different active and passive control techniques have been proposed. In the present work, the concept of breathing blunt nose (BBN) for drag reduction at hypersonic speed has been applied to a long blunt nosed body at supersonic speed. Investigation on two breathing configurations has been done using CFD tools and effect of breathing on static aerodynamic coefficients particularly on axial force coefficient has been studied. The employed breathing configurations increase normal force coefficient and pitching moment coefficient by 5% and 10% respectively. The axial force coefficient is reduced by 3.3% and 4.4% for the two breathing configurations at α=0°. The Ca reduction increases linearly with angle of attack, and it reaches 6.25% and 6.4% at α=8°. The results of non-breathing body (NBB) have been validated quantitatively using experimental data; and the results of breathing configurations match qualitatively with those found in the literature.

articleTitle: Two dimensional star grain optimization method using genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This study describes the internal ballistic and the design optimization of two-dimensional star grain of rocket motors. The burnback analysis and geometric modeling of grain geometry are calculated using star grain geometry. In this study, the grain geometry was modeled parametrically using CAD software. The internal ballistic analysis by using MATLAB program, we used zero dimensional method for calculating the performance prediction. Genetic Algorithm optimization method has been used. Average thrust maximization, total impulse maximization and minimizing the neutrality of thrust time curve under design constraints is the objective functions. The uses of Genetic Algorithm optimization method clear the problem of suitable initial guess. This idea proves increase in capability of optimal solutions. According to different objective function it is capable to choose which is suitable according to the results.

articleTitle: Effect of turbulence modeling on realistic estimation of flow characteristics of liquid ejector pump
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Ejector pumps are widely used in many industrial and engineering applications due to their simple constructions and ease of maintenance. The working fluid of ejector pump can be a gas or a liquid. When the ejectors are operated using incompressible fluids like liquids, they are often termed as Jet Pumps. One of the most important feature of these devices is that they provide the use of any ordinary centrifugal pump with a lower head but with a higher capacity, thus resulting into 2-3 folds increased mass flow rates. The realistic modeling of flow domain of ejector pump is necessary for its performance estimation and design improvements. Keeping in view the limitations and applicability of each turbulence model for specific genre of turbulent flows, the effect of RANS, modified RANS and LES modeling techniques is explored for correct estimation of flow characteristics of liquid ejector pump. In this research, the flow field of ejector pump, used in aircraft fuel system, is firstly simulated using Standard K-ε (RANS) model. The performance parameters obtained are then compared with experimental data which reveals the inadequacy of turbulence model in correct estimation of mass flow rates. For realistic modeling, the model constants are randomly tweaked to bring the simulated results closer to the experimental data. However, this methodology cannot be used for obtaining a priori simulation of subject pump. Therefore, LES is used to model the turbulent flow domain using WALE Sub Grid Scale model. The comparison of flow characteristics like turbulent eddy viscosity, Reynolds shear stresses and potential core estimation obtained from mentioned turbulence models is carried out to identify the reasons for erroneous results by Standard K-ε and to analyze the effect in turbulent flow characteristics by changing the model constants. This comparative data is overlapped with the results obtained from LES simulation to highlight the efficacy and advantages of later one in modeling the complex flow field of ejector pump.

articleTitle: Protein binding affinity prediction using support vector regression and interfecial features
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In understanding biology at the molecular level, analysis of protein interactions and protein binding affinity is a challenge. It is an important problem in computational and structural biology. Experimental measurement of binding affinity in the wet-lab is expensive and time consuming. Therefore, machine learning approaches are widely used to predict protein interactions and binding affinities by learning from specific properties of existing complexes. In this work, we propose an innovative computational model to predict binding affinities and interaction based on sequence, structural and interface features of the interacting proteins that are robust to binding associated conformational changes. We modeled the prediction of binding affinity as classification and regression problem with least-squared and support vector regression models using structure and sequence features of proteins. Specifically, we have used the number and composition of interacting residues at protein complexes interface as features and sequence features. We evaluated the performance of our prediction models using Affinity Benchmark Dataset version 2.0 which contains a diverse set of both bound and unbound protein complex structures with known binding affinities. We evaluated our regression performance results with root mean square error (RMSE) as well as Spearman and Pearson's correlation coefficients using a leave-one-out cross-validation protocol. We evaluate classification results with AUC-ROC and AUC-PR Our results show that Support Vector Regression performs significantly better than other models with a Spearman Correlation coefficient of 0.58, Pearson Correlation score of 0.55 and RMSE of 2.41 using 3-mer and sequence feature. It is interesting to note that simple features based on 3-mer features and the properties of the interface of a protein complex are predictive of its binding affinity. These features, together with support vector regression achieve higher accuracy than existing sequence based methods.

Author Keywords: Area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC-ROC)

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of virus outbreak in a computer network with limited anti-virus ability
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Numerical models play vital role in analyzing non-linear continuous dynamical systems. These models are constructed with the aim that they must behave exactly like corresponding continuous models. Present work deals with the numerical modeling of Virus Outbreak in a Computer Network with Limited Anti-Virus Ability. A competitive numerical scheme for the dynamics of a computer virus in a network has been proposed. A comparison of proposed scheme with already existing standard finite difference schemes is also presented. Standard finite difference schemes provide conditional convergence while the proposed numerical scheme is un-conditionally convergent and remains consistent with the continuous model for all parameter values.

articleTitle: Efficacy study of indigenously developed mosquito repellent BiteFree & its comparison with commercially available mosquito repellent
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Mosquitoes act as a vector for most of the life threatening diseases like malaria, yellow fever, dengue fever, chikungunya fever, filariasis, encephalitis, West Nile Virus infection, etc. It is estimated that more than 700 million people become ill each year from mosquito-transmitted disease and 3 million people die from malaria, including one child every 30 seconds. In response, numerous measures have been used to protect people from mosquitoes, such as chemical, biological, environmental and personal protection. Currently available repellents are either synthetic chemicals like Ethyle hexanediol (EHD), ethyl-3 (N-butylacetamidp) propionate (IR3535) or N, N-diethyl-m-toluamide (DEET), or plant derived chemicals such as Citronella, eucalyptus & lemongrass. The drawback of using plant-based repellents is that many of them are made up of relatively volatile constituents and are generally not effective over long periods of time. The best-known chemical insect repellent is N, N-diethyl-3-methylbenzamide (DEET). The efficacy of DEET providing a long-lasting protection of up to 8 hours from time of application against many blood feeding insects has been documented in several studies. In the present study, Bite-Free a indigenously developed mosquito repellent cream, in which active ingredient is DEET (25% w/w) was evaluated for its efficacy under controlled laboratory conditions, using arm in cage method, based on a WHO standardized procedures (WHO/HTM/NTD/WHOPES/ 2009.4) against three major disease vectors: Anopheles, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes, in comparison of its compatible, commercially available mosquito repellents, "A". The study was conducted at Centre of Excellence in Science and Technologies (CESAT), Islamabad-Pakistan from June, 2013 to June, 2016. Mosquito colonies were reared in Insectory and maintained at 27-32 °C and 60%-70% relative humidity. All collected mosquitoes were morphologically identified by using the key ZOOTAXA-589 (2004) under stereomicroscope model No.1106. Approximately 200 adult mosquitoes aged 7 to 10 days old were used in this trial. Before the beginning of study, informed consent was obtained from all volunteers. During the trial all volunteers were monitored for possible side-effects of the repellent. A medical doctor was on hand during the trials to respond to any side effects. Protective Efficacy of BiteFree was found 91.5% & protection time was 6-7 hours and no any side effect was observed during trials. While Protective Efficacy of commercially available mosquito repellent reference lotion "A" was 86.4% & protection time was 6-7 hours. Irritation and redness of skin were noted in few subjects. Shelf life of BiteFree was 03 years and reference lotion "A" shelf life was found one year.

articleTitle: The application of particles image velocimetry technique in the measurement of steady-state flow velocity fields for coolant of a model of reactor vessel downcomer
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: The aim of this work is to study how steady-state flow will be visualized in different locations at Harbin Engineering University (HEU) vessel down-comer which designed by The College of Nuclear Science and Technology at HEU. PIV technique used to quantify the flow velocities at different locations (5 cm, 10cm) under the inlet location, at the downcomer of the Reactor vessel model. The application of the Particle Image Velocimetry technique to the study of velocity distribution in the reactor vessel downcomer presented. To analyze the velocities in the reactor vessel downcomer, a steady state single-phase flow distribution is required. An experimental setup designed to assist in the characterization of steady state flow problems in Reactor vessel model described. Two different inlet flow-rates applied in the loop. The images of the experiments were captured by, CCD camera. The given images processed on Matlab program. The Post-processing of the PIV data gave quantitative results of good quality. From the visualization of the results, it is clearly to be seen, the velocity flow vectors split and distributed around the inner cylinder, starting from the inlet position and it downwards in the region opposite to inlet position. For velocity measurement, the magnitude of the steady-state velocity at 5 and 10 cm is almost 0.130 m/s when the inlet flow-rate was 0.29 m/s, and 0.129m/s for 0.26 m/s inlet flow rate. According to the results, The PIV technique proves to quantify the velocities of the coolant in reactor vessel downcomer.

articleTitle: Sampled-data robust feedback linearization using higher order sliding mode observer
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In this work a robust feedback linearization scheme for minimum phase systems using sampled-data configuration is presented. A discrete-time observer implementation for sliding mode observer based on Euler approximation is presented. The observer using system output, simultaneously estimates drift term and system-states while operating in discrete-time domain. Unmodeled system dynamics and disturbances are compensated using estimated drift term in feedback. Also, discrete controller is designed using Emulation Design procedure. Computer simulations are used to investigate performance of presented feedback linearization configuration in tracking applications of DC motor and magnetic levitation systems. Simulations show that on increasing sampling period, performance of discrete observer degrades more for faster changing system dynamics, then as compared to slower changing system dynamics. The discrete observer also demonstrates good performance in case of system parameters perturbation, or in presence of disturbance.

articleTitle: Study of aerodynamic coefficients dependency on reynolds number for subsonic flow conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Aerodynamic coefficients play a key role to determine the behavior of a flying vehicle along its trajectory for a particular mission. Prediction of these aerodynamics coefficients can be made through experiments, analytical solution or Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). These coefficients are determined for a wide range of Mach numbers and angles of attack at different altitudes. During flight, Mach numbers may be similar at two (or more) different altitudes. However, Reynolds number can be different at each altitude due to the variation of density and temperature with altitude. In present work, the dependency of aerodynamic coefficients on Reynolds number is studied for subsonic flow conditions. For this purpose, simulations are performed on 3D half body of HB-1 test case with 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order coupled steady state solver and k-ω SST turbulence model. Simulations are performed for Mach numbers 0.6 and 0.8 for altitudes (sea level to 70 km) and angles of attack. Axial force, normal force and pitching moment coefficients are determined. Results show that axial force coefficient varies significantly with Reynolds number for a fixed Mach number. Variation in normal force and pitching moment coefficient is insignificant for smaller values of angle of attack. However, at larger values variations are significant. Results show that low subsonic regimes are more affected by Reynolds number. For validation purpose numerical results are also compared with experimental data of HB-1 test case.

articleTitle: Development of error decoder for monopulse auto-tracking system
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: This paper presents the design and results of error decoder for monopulse auto-tracking receiver. The presented error decoder is specifically designed for antenna systems where errors are sent as a composite signal over a single coaxial wire from the feed source mounted on a parabolic dish. Errors are modulated locally as AM on LNA as the envelope of the PCM/FM received signal. The coaxial simultaneously carries error and data signals from which the error decoder exclusively calculates azimuth and elevation error voltages and drives the corresponding servos of the antenna system. The design of error decoder along with the performance results for tests conducted in the anechoic chamber are presented in the following text.

articleTitle: The effects of shear flows on thermal instability of viscoelastic fluids in a fluid-porous system
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: A mathematical model is set up to describe natural convection in a two-layer system with effects of a plane shear flows and a constant flux heating in the case of a viscoelastic fluid. Through theoretical analysis and numerical simulation, the results will be obtained to explain and predict the physical phenomena of thermal instability. A linear stability analysis will be used to get eigenvalue problems for a plane shear flow. Then, a spectral method will be adopted to compute the neutral curves in thermal convection with the effects of shear flows and viscoelastic fluids. With the help of numerical simulation, it shows that neutral curves have a bi-modal nature for a proper fluid-porous depth ratio. Transverse rolls generated by shear flows are studied as well as longitudinal rolls. The effects of viscoelastic fluids on thermal instability will also be investigated in this paper. For Newtonian fluids, longitudinal rolls always set in before transvers rolls. Transvers rolls under the effects of viscoelastic fluids may be observed early in the flow phenomena.

articleTitle: Analysis on drag characteristic of busemann-type biplane
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Reducing wave drag caused by shock wave is one of the biggest challenge for supersonic aircraft. Busemann-type biplane could remarkably reduce wave drag by the interaction of shock and expansion waves. Using the Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) analysis methodology, the drag characteristic of Busemann-type biplane is investigated. For inviscid flow, the Busemann biplane can reduce wave drag near to zero. In case of viscous flow, affected by surface friction, there is an increase in the drag coefficient of the Busemann biplane. However, the increase is still less than half of the contrasted diamond airfoil's drag. The diamond airfoil chord length and thickness are the same as the Busemann biplane. The Busemann biplane has low drag characteristic at its designed Mach number. During the process of speeding up, the mass flow is choked between the biplane resulting in sharp increase in the drag. To resolve the flow chocking problem, a methodology is presented that combines dislocating biplane with deflecting slat and flap. This could change the inlet-to-throat ratio and pressure distribution to reduce the drag penalty. The resulting drag coefficient is considerably small compared to the original Busemann biplane and the diamond airfoil.

articleTitle: Optimization of bottom-up saliency detection through gram polynomial decimation
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Conspicuous objects in a particular scene grab human attention which subsequently avoid surroundings from being processed in detail. This hypothesis is modelled as saliency detection algorithms which have found vast range of applications from object tracking to data compression. This paper presents an optimization technique for bottom-up saliency detection algorithm based on Gram polynomial decimation. Gram polynomial basis offer more effective decimation of images as compared to Fourier basis by suppressing Gibbs error. The technique has been validated on MSRA10k Salient Object Database using Itti's method, graph based method, spectral residual approach and frequency-tuned method. Results show significant performance boost in terms of higher F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> score and reduced computation time.

articleTitle: Flutter analysis of ARW-2 wing using doublet lattice
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: Aeroelastic characteristics of an aeroplane are of important concern in the design of modern elastic aircrafts, which must be considered in the preliminary design. This paper is about the investigation of aeroelastic effects in the subsonic speed range and the flutter analysis of a large elastic wing known as the DAST ARW-2. The normal frequencies and mode shapes are evaluated and used for the aeroelastic analysis. The modal frequencies and mode shapes showed no significant difference and showed good agreement with experimental results. Vertical and torsional linear deflections due to applied loads were validated with the previous results. The wing structure is modeled using composites cited in literature. Flutter properties of wing are characterized by a non-dimensional quantity known as flutter speed index (FSI). The results have been validated by comparison with the flutter data of ARW-2 using Doublet lattice method. The Flutter speed index (FSI) values show good agreement with literature results.

articleTitle: Study the effect of B-site dopant on dielectric properties of lead free piezoceramics with high curie temperature
publicationTitle: 2018 15th International Bhurban Conference on Applied Sciences and Technology (IBCAST)
abstract: In the present work effect of Nb doping on dielectric properties of BNT was studied. ((Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>.<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">05x</inf>Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>.<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> with × = 0 to 0.08) was synthesized by conventional solid state reaction technique. The effect of Nb doping was investigated for x= 0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06 & 0.08 mol. Calcination was done at 870°C. XRD analysis of calcined powders confirms the formation of rhombohedral structure.
